newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assembly passes skateboard liability bill.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assembly passes skateboard liability bill.

text.p: The California State Assembly Friday passed a bill to protect cities from being sued by skateboarders injured on public property.

The bill proposes adding skateboarding to a list of activities including mountain bicycling, boating, rope swinging, tree climbing, cross-country skiing and surfing, from which the law currently protects cities and other public entities from liability.
It was passed in the Assembly by a 58-9 vote and will now go on to a State Senate vote.

"No longer is (skateboarding) limited to just jumping off sidewalk curbs," said Bill Morrow, a Republican Assembly member who authored the bill. "Today the sport includes all kinds of dangerous acrobatic and airborne stunts that place the skateboarder in danger of serious injury and the local community in fear of a lawsuit."
As with other sporting activities from which cities have protection from lawsuits, skateboarders could still bring lawsuits against the city in limited circumstances.

An aide to Morrow said cities could be sued if they are negligent in maintaining areas set up specifically for skateboarding, or if the injury occurs in an area in which the city charged an admission fee.
But he said the bill would do away with the vast majority of lawsuits by skateboarders injured through their own recklessness.

Many cities frustrated by the nuisance of skateboarders in public streets and parks, have looked into containing the activity by setting up so-called skateboarding parks, but have feared such a move would increase their liability.
